paragraphs.text: Volcanic eruptions can affect the global climate. When Mount Pinatubo in the Philippines erupted in 1991, it released millions of tonnes of sulphur dioxide into the upper atmosphere.
The gas formed tiny droplets that reflected sunlight back into space. As a result, average global temperatures fell by about half a degree Celsius over the following two years.
Some scientists have proposed copying this effect deliberately to slow global warming, by spraying similar particles into the atmosphere from aircraft.
Critics warn that such geoengineering could disrupt rainfall patterns, and that once started, it would have to continue for decades to avoid sudden warming.
